Phase 11 is done: the app has no Java left. Commit 23198873 passed CI, and I built this phase on top of it.

From the repository root, run this first to delete the old files:

sh
git rm app/src/main/java/app/simple/positional/model/Measure.java app/src/main/java/app/simple/positional/model/MeasurePoint.java app/src/main/java/app/simple/positional/model/TrailEntry.java app/src/main/java/app/simple/positional/model/TrailPoint.java app/src/main/java/app/simple/positional/extensions/maps/MapsCallbacks.java app/src/main/java/app/simple/positional/decorations/interpolators/LatLngInterpolator.java app/src/main/java/app/simple/positional/decorations/utils/CircleUtils.java app/src/main/java/app/simple/positional/decorations/utils/MarkerUtils.java app/databases/schemas/app.simple.positional.database.instances.TrailDataDatabase/2.json app/databases/schemas/app.simple.positional.database.instances.TrailDataDatabase/3.json
Then extract positional-phase11.tar.gz at the repository root. It holds only the 24 new or changed files.

What changed

Saved data: The four Room models (measures, measure points, trails, trail points) are now Kotlin. Their columns and which columns may be empty are unchanged, so measures and trails already on your Nord should open as before. Some screens now treat empty names and notes explicitly, but they display the same as before.
Map callbacks: I removed the callbacks that no panel used: line count, target updated, touch, navigate and target add.
Google map animations: The marker, accuracy circle and measure line animations are now Kotlin. The shared position and heading calculations live in MapInterpolation.
Bug fix: The Google map’s accuracy circle animated its radius as if it were an angle. Any accuracy above 360 m wrapped around and showed the wrong size.
Cleanup: I removed an unused function in Angle.kt and two schema files left over from a database class that no longer exists.
Tests: New tests cover the map calculations, the circle radius fix and how measure points are stored and read back.
CI: A new step fails the build if the saved database schema signature changes. That catches a model change that would make Room refuse to open existing databases.
README: Phase 11 is marked done. Phase 12 is next: replace LiveData with StateFlow in the two remaining view models, and share code between the three Google map views.
As before, I couldn’t run Gradle here because Google’s Maven servers are blocked. I compiled and ran the new calculation and conversion code with a standalone Kotlin compiler. The Room code generation and the Android build will first run in CI.
